title: Three presentations at the 2026 BMES Annual Meeting in Orlando
text:
The lab presents its work at the 2026 BMES Annual Meeting in Orlando:
• Gut microbiome reshapes oral drug pharmacokinetics through coupled host-transporter remodeling and direct bacterial metabolism
• The Silent Metabolite Problem: Gut Bacteria Evade Standard Detection Across IBD and Colorectal Cancer
• Gut Microbial Regulation of Notch Dynamics in the Colon (Ishita Dasgupta)
Abhinav Bhushan also chairs two sessions: AI for Genomics, Molecular Design & Cellular Systems, and Imaging in Cancer.

title: Abhinav Bhushan joins the Editorial Board of Scientific Reports
text: Abhinav Bhushan has joined the Editorial Board of Scientific Reports.

title: Quoted in the Deccan Herald on algae and plastic pollution
text: Abhinav Bhushan was quoted in the Deccan Herald article “Can algae become a solution to the plastic pollution crisis?”

title: Invited talk at the ANRF International Workshop
text: Abhinav Bhushan presented “Engineering Adaptive Microphysiological Systems with Machine Learning and Biosensors” at the ANRF International Workshop, From Design to Detection: Targeted Drug Delivery Crossing Biological Barriers and AI-Driven Biosensors.

title: Three new graduate students join the lab!
text: We are excited to welcome Liya Patel, Jaime Greatorex and Maria Tereza Cohen Bichara to the lab.

title: Digital Futures Scholar-in-Residence in Stockholm
text: Abhinav Bhushan joined KTH Royal Institute of Technology and Stockholm University in Sweden as a Digital Futures Scholar-in-Residence (visiting researcher), hosted by Dr. Erica Zeglio.

title: Keynote at the Digital Futures Workshop in Stockholm
text: Abhinav Bhushan gave the keynote, “Integrated microfluidic organ models and biosensors for intelligent disease modeling,” at the Digital Futures Workshop on Fabrication and Integration of Bioelectronic Sensors at Stockholm University.

title: New paper on bile salts and E. coli colonization in colorectal cancer organoids
text: Ishita Dasgupta and colleagues report how bile salts and bacterial bile salt hydrolase activity influence E. coli colonization and FXR signaling in organoids. Published in Annals of Biomedical Engineering. Congratulations to all!
image_alt: Brightfield image of an organoid with fluorescent bacteria nearby

title: Preprint: an AI algorithm for designing synthetic promoters
text: Our paper on an AI algorithm for the design and analysis of synthetic promoters is now available as a preprint.

title: Invited talk at the IBTN Symposium, UIC
text: We were invited to present our research on organ-on-chips and sensors at the IBTN Symposium at the University of Illinois Chicago. We are thankful for the invitation.

title: New NSF funding for closed-loop control of a liver microphysiological system
text: The lab receives new NSF funding to engineer closed-loop control of a liver microphysiological system. We are very thankful for the support and excited to continue our work in this area.

title: Invited visit to Amity University, Delhi
text: The lab was invited to present its research at Amity University in Delhi, India. We thank the faculty for hosting us and for the delightful conversations, and we look forward to collaborating.

title: Dahee Chung wins second place for her ResMatch project
text: Dahee Chung won second place for her ResMatch project, “Functional and genomic clustering in the colon.” Congratulations!

title: iGEM team SynBeeGees wins a Silver medal in Paris
text: Students from the “Engineering Life” IPRO and student club presented their project, SynBeeGees, at the iGEM meeting in Paris. The team won a Silver medal. Congratulations to all!

title: Four presentations at the 2025 BMES Annual Meeting
text:
We presented our work at the 2025 BMES Annual Meeting in San Diego:
• A Cross-Evaluation of Generative AI’s Role in BME Medical Device Concept Generation 
• Modeling drug kinetics under microgravity 
• Real-Time Control of Microfluidic Mixing via Machine Learning Driven Prediction 
• Colon Organoids on-a-Chip to Study the Influence of Bile Acids on Bacterial Colonization

title: Preprint: bile salts and bacterial colonization in colorectal organoids
text: Our paper on colorectal organoids and bile salts is now available as a preprint. Congratulations to all!

title: Electronic-nose signatures in nasopharyngeal swab samples
text: Our paper on measuring volatile organic compounds in viral transport media, and the mathematical algorithms to analyze them, is published in PLOS One. A big congratulations to our colleagues at Rush University.

title: Summer researchers from Spain and BIT Mesra win awards
text: The lab hosted one student from Spain and seven from BIT Mesra this summer. They carried out three projects on machine learning and AI, and all three won awards at the summer research symposium. Congratulations to everyone!

title: Sustainable Synthesizers wins the Dean's Choice Award
text: The Sustainable Synthesizers project from the iGEM IPRO class won the Dean's Choice Award at Illinois Tech's Innovation Day. Congratulations to all!

title: Guests from industry and the clinic visit the Medical Devices course
text: Monica Vajani from mHub, Rachael Menhart from Boston Scientific and Dr. Margot Damaser from the Cleveland Clinic visited the Medical Devices course to share their experiences and insights with students.

title: Ishita Dasgupta presents at the 2024 BMES Annual Meeting
text: Ishita made her first presentation at the 2024 BMES Annual Meeting in Baltimore. Congratulations!

title: Talk on ethics in biomedical innovation
text: Abhinav Bhushan was invited to give a Responsible Conduct of Research talk, “Ethics in Biomedical Innovation,” at Illinois Tech's Center for the Study of Ethics in the Professions.

title: Illinois Tech award for engagement with students and organizations
text: Abhinav Bhushan received Illinois Tech's Achievement of Commitment for Engagement with Students and Organizations.

title: Summer researchers from Panama, BIT Mesra and Illinois Tech
text: The lab hosted three students from Panama and one from BIT Mesra this summer. Together with an Illinois Tech computer science undergraduate, they carried out research on machine learning and AI and presented their work. Congratulations to everyone!

title: Review: engineered bacteria for detecting and treating colorectal cancer
text: With collaborators at UC San Diego, a review of engineered bacterial therapeutics for colorectal cancer. Published in Trends in Cancer. Congratulations to all!

title: How gut bacteria change the pharmacokinetics of tacrolimus and sulfasalazine
text: Our multiyear study shows how bacteria influence the pharmacokinetics of tacrolimus and sulfasalazine by regulating host metabolism. Published in Advanced Therapeutics.

title: Workshop: Engineering Biology using Microfluidics
text: The lab ran a summer workshop on engineering biology using microfluidics (BIOMIC 2024) for undergraduate students from the City Colleges of Chicago and Illinois Tech. Thank you to the NSF for the funding that made it possible.

title: Review: organ-on-chip models of mucosal tissues and vasculature
text: Ishita Dasgupta and colleagues review how microfluidic organ-on-chip technology is changing models of mucosal tissues and blood vessels. Published in Bioengineering. Congratulations to all!

title: Oral Health and Policy Research Symposium
text: The lab took part in the 2024 Oral Health and Policy Research Symposium on the University of Chicago campus.

title: Leading a team at an ML/AI codeathon for biological research
text: We will lead a group at the Building Transparent ML/AI Solutions to Advance Biological Research Codeathon. The project will build machine learning and AI models to predict the role of bacteria in host function.

title: NSF CAREER Award
text: Abhinav Bhushan received a Faculty Early Career Development (CAREER) Award from the National Science Foundation.

title: Interview with The Scientist on disease scent signatures
text: Abhinav Bhushan was interviewed by The Scientist for “Disease Scent Signatures Disclose What the Nose Knows.”

title: Video: a nasal epithelial cell spun by its cilia
text: A nasal epithelial cell rotating, driven by its oscillating cilia.

title: Review: linear and nonlinear models in breath analysis
text: Our review of the linear and nonlinear models used to analyze breath with the Cyranose 320 electronic nose was accepted in the Journal of Breath Research. Congratulations to all!

title: NSF PREPARE podcast interview
text: Our interview for NSF PREPARE: Science Before the Storm is available as a downloadable podcast.

title: Commentary: modeling collective cell behavior in cancer
text: Our commentary, “Modeling collective cell behavior in cancer: perspectives from an interdisciplinary conversation,” is published in Cell Systems. Congratulations to all!

title: Collaborative R21 with Rush on personalized pancreatic cancer
text: Our collaborative R21 with Rush University on personalized pancreatic cancer using microfluidic organ-on-chip devices received its notice of award.

title: Review: VOC profiling for noninfectious diseases
text: Our review of the diagnostic potential of volatile organic compound profiling for noninfectious diseases was accepted in BME Frontiers. Congratulations to all!

title: Illinois Tech News features the lab's colon chip
text: The story describes how the lab uses a microfluidic device to test engineered bacteria designed to detect and eliminate colon cancer cells, in an NIH-funded project led by UC San Diego.

title: CMBE Young Innovator Award
text: Abhinav Bhushan was named a Cellular and Molecular Bioengineering Young Innovator by the Biomedical Engineering Society. Credit goes to all the students who carried out the studies.

title: How an anoxic environment shapes bacterial regulation of intestinal function
text: Our latest paper, “Causative Role of Anoxic Environment in Bacterial Regulation of Human Intestinal Function,” is published in Cellular and Molecular Bioengineering. Congratulations, everyone!

title: Funding to develop a point-of-care device for periodontitis
text: The group receives new funding from the Institute for Translational Medicine to develop a point-of-care device for periodontitis.

title: Preprint: the SARS-CoV-2 spike protein and inflammation in lung and intestinal cells
text: A new preprint from our NSF collaborative project with Rush University Medical Center: “SARS-CoV-2 S1 Spike Protein Promotes MAPK and NF-kB Activation and Inflammatory Cytokine Production in Human Lung and Intestinal Epithelial Cells.”

title: Patient-derived pancreatic cancer-on-a-chip
text: Our paper with Rush University Medical Center, “Patient-derived pancreatic cancer-on-a-chip recapitulates the tumor microenvironment,” is accepted for publication in Microsystems & Nanoengineering. Congratulations, everyone!

title: Contributing to the decadal survey on research in space
text: The lab contributed to the National Academies' Decadal Survey on Biological and Physical Sciences Research in Space 2023–2032.

title: Investigating insulin resistance with a multiorgan organ-on-chip
text: Our paper, “Investigation of insulin resistance through a multiorgan microfluidic organ-on-chip,” is accepted for publication in Biomedical Materials. Congratulations, everyone!

title: New NIH R01 to diagnose periodontitis at the point of care
text: In this collaborative R01 project we will develop a microfluidic point-of-care device and combine it with machine learning to diagnose periodontitis.

title: New NIH U01 to engineer native E. coli against colorectal cancer
text: The collaborative U01 project will engineer native E. coli to detect, report and treat colorectal cancer.

title: Hasan Abdelsaid and Michael Watts named ResMatch fellows
text: Hasan Abdelsaid (BME) and Michael Watts (Biology) were selected as ResMatch fellows for Fall 2021.

title: Review: organ-chip models for precision medicine in pancreatic cancer
text: Our review, “Organ-Chip models: Opportunities for precision medicine in pancreatic cancer,” is published in Cancers.

title: Pooja Patel, Phuong Tran and Jessica Rodriguez Arias named ResMatch fellows
text: Pooja Patel, Phuong Tran and Jessica Rodriguez Arias were selected as ResMatch fellows for Summer 2021.

title: An organ-chip with a partitioned-oxygen intestinal microenvironment
text: Our paper on creating a partitioned-oxygen intestinal microenvironment in a microfluidic organ-chip is published in FASEB Journal.

title: New NSF funding profiled
text: Illinois Tech News profiles our new NSF-funded research on volatile organic compounds, which could lead to a rapid diagnostic test for COVID-19.

title: A 3D human adipose tissue model in a microfluidic device
text: Our collaborative paper with the University of Texas at San Antonio and the University of Chicago on a 3D human adipose tissue microfluidic construct is published in Lab on a Chip.

title: Toward an insulin-resistant adipose model on a chip
text: Our latest paper on an insulin-resistant adipocyte model on a chip is published in Cellular and Molecular Bioengineering.

title: Undergraduate research on leaky gut published
text: Undergraduate student Jasmine Baste's preliminary research on leaky gut is published in an undergraduate research journal!

title: Funding for biosensors to detect amyloid proteins in Alzheimer's disease
text: The lab receives new funding to develop ultrasensitive protein biosensors that detect amyloid proteins in patients with Alzheimer's disease.

title: New NSF funding for SARS-CoV-2 research
text: The lab receives new funding from the NSF to understand cell biology related to SARS-CoV-2 infection and to develop sensors that detect early infection.

title: Abstract at the American Diabetes Association Scientific Sessions
text: Our abstract was presented at the 80th Scientific Sessions of the American Diabetes Association.

title: Nida Tanataweethum's abstract named Outstanding at ENDO 2020
text: Nida's abstract received an Outstanding Abstract Award at the Endocrine Society's ENDO 2020 meeting. Congratulations!

title: Congratulations to the class of 2020!
Jasmine Baste wins first prize at the IL-LSAMP conference
text: Jasmine received first prize for her poster presentation at the IL-LSAMP conference.

title: NSF I-Corps Site/Node grant
text: Abhinav Bhushan received an NSF I-Corps Site/Node grant, part of the lab's work to assess the market fit of a technology developed in the lab.

title: Student team competes at iGEM 2019 in Boston
text: Our student team took part in the 2019 iGEM competition in Boston. The project also won first place in its category at IPRO Day.

title: Jasmine Baste receives an ABRCMS travel award
text: Jasmine received a travel award to present her work at ABRCMS.

title: Feipeng Yang becomes the lab's first PhD graduate
text: Feipeng Yang defended his dissertation to graduate as the lab's first PhD student.

title: Pilot funding with Rush for personalized pancreatic cancer diagnosis
text: Our collaborative project with Rush received pilot funding for personalized pancreatic cancer diagnosis.

title: Funding from ARDF
text: The lab receives funding from ARDF!

title: BIT Mesra students join for the Summer Immersion Program
text: Students from BIT Mesra work in the lab as part of the Illinois Tech Summer Immersion Program. Welcome!

title: Four MS thesis defenses
text: Qifan He, Laura Hetzel, Vineet Penumarthy and Kihwan Kim successfully defended their MS theses. Congratulations!

title: Team selected for the NAE Grand Challenges Scholars Program
text: A team mentored by Abhinav Bhushan was selected to represent Illinois Tech in the 2019 National Academy of Engineering Grand Challenges Scholars Program in Washington, D.C.

title: Real-time measurement of cholesterol secreted by liver cells
text: Our paper, “Real-time measurement of cholesterol secreted by human hepatocytes using a novel microfluidic assay,” is published in Technology, with a press release and further coverage.

title: Andrea Cancino receives a BMES travel award
text: Andrea received a BMES travel award to attend the 2018 BMES Annual Meeting in Atlanta.

title: Poster at the Islet Cell Biology meeting
text: A poster on our research was presented at the Islet Cell Biology meeting in Nashville.

title: Rongfei Fu defends his thesis
text: Rongfei Fu successfully defended his thesis. Congratulations!

title: Chengyao Wang receives a travel award to the Kenneth Rainin Innovation Symposium
text: Chengyao received a travel award to attend the Kenneth Rainin Innovation Symposium in San Francisco and presented two posters there.

title: Illinois Tech profiles the lab's obesity research
text: Illinois Tech News profiles how the lab's microfluidic chip is advancing obesity research.

title: Technology Networks profiles our colon-on-a-chip
text: Technology Networks profiles our work on a collagen membrane that improves the function of a colon-on-a-chip.

title: Chengyao Wang receives the Starr Fieldhouse Research Fellowship
text: Congratulations, Chengyao!

title: A primary murine adipose tissue-chip
text: Nida Tanataweethum's paper, “Establishment and characterization of a primary murine adipose tissue-chip,” is accepted for publication in Biotechnology and Bioengineering.

title: A microfluidic colon with an extracellular matrix membrane
text: Chengyao Wang's paper is accepted for publication in ACS Biomaterials Science & Engineering, with additional coverage by ACS.

title: Science outreach with C2ST and Science Riot
text: The lab communicates science to the public, this time through a partnership with C2ST and Science Riot.

title: A microfluidic in-line ELISA for measuring secreted proteins
text: Our paper, “A microfluidic in-line ELISA for measuring secreted proteins under perfusion,” is published in Biomedical Microdevices.

title: Selected for Phase 2 of the Nayar Prize II
text: The lab is one of the two teams selected for Phase 2 of Illinois Tech's Nayar Prize II.

title: Talk at the Mid-Atlantic Diabetes Symposium at NIH
text: Abhinav Bhushan presented at the Mid-Atlantic Diabetes Symposium held at NIH in Bethesda.

title: Sonali Karnik and Nida Tanataweethum present at Experimental Biology 2017
text: Dr. Karnik and Nida presented their research at the Experimental Biology 2017 conference.

Tung Nguyen presents a first-author poster at Pittcon 2017
